dids.notes: Only updates with ignition on. An early reading: raw 0x8996 = 68.79 %, dashboard showed 68 %.

Three 32-bit counters. Word 0: energy into the battery including regeneration, 1/16 kWh. Over a DC fast charge it grew 23.06 kWh against 23.68 kWh on the charger (2026-10-11, 27.6 -> 83.6 %, snap_20261011_082224 -> _091220), and 0.375 kWh over a 9 km drive without charging (watch_bms_20261011_091702). Word 1: energy out of the battery, 1/16 kWh: +68.4 kWh over 341 km is 20.1 kWh/100 km against 19.5 on the trip computer (2026-10-05 to 2026-10-10); +2.06 kWh on the 9 km drive; +1 count over the 2026-10-05/06 charge (+134 over the night of 2026-10-02/03, cause not known). Word 2: the odometer 0xD49C + 9 km in all 39 snaps. Word 0 reads 0 after the car wakes until it has driven or charged (26 of 83 snaps 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-11, also 15 min in Ready standing on 2026-10-12); word 1 never reads 0. The dashboard then leaves the energy into the battery empty. The dashboard reads words 0 and 1 as lifetime_charged_kwh and lifetime_discharged_kwh.

Counts seconds. About 108.5 million s (3.4 years); the BMS manufacture date 0xF18B is 8.1.2023, 3.7 years before. Not the same counter as 0xD4CA, which runs in 0.1 s steps from a different starting point. Against the snap times it gained 661 s (11 min) in 7 days (2026-09-29 to 2026-10-06): within a session it keeps to wall time, the gains fall between sessions (e.g. +142 s between 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-05). 0xD4CA kept to wall time within 2 s over the same days. Own scan 2026-09-26.

60391424 -> 60398592 over the 7 km drive of 2026-09-26 (see the VCU 0xD49C) = 58976.0 -> 58983.0 km. The low bits were zero both times, so the extra resolution may not be used. OBDb Peugeot-208 divides by 1000; that gives 60391 km against 58976 km on the dashboard, so /1024 is right for this car.

Listed as SOC by wican-fw#278 without an expression. Same /512 scale as 0xD410 but moves on its own: equal raw bytes (0x8996) in one reading, 0x88F7 = 68.48 % some minutes later (scan of the 0xD8xx range, 2026-09-26 10:30 UTC). OBDb Peugeot-208 gives it as 208_HVBAT_SOC_RAW, /512. Checked against 0xD410 in 83 snaps 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-11 over 27.6-99.9 %: slope 0.998, rms 0.11 points, at most 0.42 apart. It runs ahead of 0xD410: about 0.25 points higher while DC charging (2026-10-11), up to 0.4 points lower while driving (2026-10-07), consistent with an unfiltered value.

2026-09-26 10:30 UTC (scan of the 0xD8xx range, before the readings at 41 % that afternoon): raw 0x19ED = 414.81 V with cells at 3.82-3.84 V. 414.81 / 3.83 = 108.3, consistent with 108 cells in series. Battery-Emulator adds 80 V for its 'MysteryVan' pack; OBDb and evDash /16 fit this car.

Offset 76800 (= 1200 x 64), 1/64 A per count, discharge positive. Checked 2026-09-26 with a 228 s live recording in Ready (heater on/off): power x time gave 0.225 kWh, the energy counter 0xD865 fell 0.219 kWh and SOC fell 0.525 % (= 0.235 kWh of 44.7 kWh usable). Battery-Emulator uses 0.0155 A per count with the same offset (0.8 % from 1/64); evDash uses 0.018 A with the opposite sign, which gave 15-18 % too much energy. Heater alone about 5-7 kW flat out; with the heater off (LO, fan on) 1.2-1.3 kW remained. 2026-10-02, two 28 km drives: power x time 3.922 and 3.890 kWh against the energy counter 0xD865 falling 3.938 and 4.172 kWh. The first matches; on the second the BMS SOC (and with it 0xD865) fell about 7 % faster than the integrated current, so the counter, not this scale, is the likelier cause.

So the columns look like 10 °C pack temperature bands; what the rows stand for is open.

blocks.why: Run these first as a sanity check. If the ECU serial number and software version come back as readable text and SOC returns a plausible percentage, the transport is proven and everything after this is the car's behaviour, not a bug.

The densest cluster: most pack values live here - 0xD81x live measurements, 0xD86x capacity, health and cell extremes, 0xD87x temperatures and power limits on the BMS; pack temperatures and HV voltage around 0xD8Ex on the VCU; 12 V and HV voltages, grid voltage and charge cable flags around 0xD80x-0xD85x on the charger.

Vehicle-level state rather than pack internals: 0xD402 speed (VCU), 0xD410 calibrated SOC (BMS), 0xD434 ambient temperature (VCU), 0xD49C odometer, plus the per-cell arrays at 0xD440/0xD442 on the BMS. The dashboard range estimate is not here.
Standardised by ISO 14229, so it is the same on every manufacturer and mostly ASCII. Self-describing: part numbers, software versions, manufacturing date. Low value but zero interpretation work.

The whole manufacturer D block. On the tested car it found groups not documented in the listed sources: D5xx-D7xx on the VCU, DCxx and DFxx on the BMS, DCxx on the motor controller and 0xD5BD/0xD5CF-0xD5D2 on the charger.
blocks.runtime: about 10 minutes per ECU (measured 9 min 50 s)

blocks.why: Catches anything outside the expected groupings. Run it twice and diff the results - a missing response is not the same as a non-existent identifier, and silence under load produces false negatives.

cautions: Read-only. The program sends only services 0x22, 0x24, 0x19 and 0x3E. Never send 0x14 (clears diagnostic history) or 0x31 (RoutineControl).
Do not attempt 0x27 SecurityAccess. Wrong keys lock the ECU for a delay that can survive a power cycle. NRC 0x33 means leave it alone.
On some cars, actively querying with the ignition off triggers the alarm system. Reported on forums for other platforms, not for e-CMP itself.
Long scans keep the car awake. In an EV the 12 V battery is what drains, and a flat 12 V means the car will not start at all. Keep it in Ready or on charge.
Broadcast sniffing worked on a 2020 Corsa-e even with ignition off, but newer models broadcast much less.

Do not sweep CAN IDs below 0x600 on e-CMP. A TesterPresent sweep of 0x500-0x5FF on 2026-09-27 stored P17CC-62 on the VCU and U1313-83 on the power steering (stored, not active), stamped with the minute of the sweep: some IDs there are ordinary application messages. The 0x5CA "ECU" it seemed to find was one of those messages. Known diagnostic IDs below 0x600, like the charger 0x590, are safe to address directly. P17CC-62 was not stored on the VCU on 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-04; U1313-83 was still stored on the power steering.
